title: Design an approximately inertial experiment
promptMarkdown: Two freely falling test masses near a spherical body have initial transverse separation $L=12\,\mathrm m$ and zero relative velocity. Use $g=8.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $R=4.0\times10^6\,\mathrm m$, and regard $g/R$ as constant. Derive the leading separation change after $3.0\,\mathrm s$. A detector resolves $5.0\,\mu\mathrm m$: is neglecting tides justified? Find the largest leading-order duration for a shift below that resolution. Repeat the sign and factor for a radial pair. Explain why neither test mass needs a nonzero accelerometer reading.
hintLadder: Use the transverse eigenvalue of the field gradient.
Integrate relative acceleration twice, using the initial relative velocity.
Solve a displacement bound, not an acceleration bound.
